title: Blues in the country and plantation guitarists
summary: They played Memphis Blues with Gabriel; the blues came a year or two after he started; plantation guitarists.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: I was gonna ask, up in the country, the blues up there, did they have much blues? The Gabriel Band, did you ever play blues with them?
Yeah, we played blues, Memphis Blues. Memphis Blues, yeah, Memphis Blues, you know. And we had another blues used to go, Memphis.
And you remember when the blues came in, or did they always have the blues when you were a boy?
Well, no, I believe the blues came in about a year or two after I started playing. You didn't know nothing about the blues.
I wondered on the plantation up there, if there were many people just played guitar and would sing the blues by themselves?
Yeah, I used to have Adam Lombay, Adam Lombay and Naveel, my cousin, who used to play.
Did they do that before you started, or after you were a musician?
Well, they used to do that during my young days. Didn't have many musicians out there at that time, you know?
What would you call that kind of music that they would sing and play on the guitar like that? Was there any special name for that kind of music?
Well, no. No, just the make up.
Yeah. Spanish, you know. Spanish style or something?
